title: Hakluyt Society Research Grants
eligibility_summary: Researchers preparing publication proposals for the Society, or working on proposals already approved and under contract to the Society. Recipients need not be members of the Society. No nationality restriction stated; funded from the Society's Harry & Grace Smith Fund.
summary: Reimburses agreed research expenditure in two categories: (A) research supporting preparation of publication projects for submission to the Society; (B) research toward completion of publication projects already under contract. Payments made as reimbursement of previously-agreed expenditure via the series editors.
discipline_tags: history of exploration;history of travel;maritime history;cartography;cultural encounter
notes: Rolling research-support scheme with no fixed deadline and no stated amount (reimbursement of agreed expenditure, capped by the Harry & Grace Smith Fund). Page is undated as to closing and describes an ongoing standing offer, so treated as rolling/open per inclusion rule. Tightly tied to the Society's own publication pipeline (applications under A go to the Administrator, under B to the assigned Series Editor). FLAG FOR REVIEW: eligibility is effectively restricted to people working on a Hakluyt Society volume/proposal - arguably borderline as a general 'research grant' available to UK researchers; kept in_scope=yes because it is a genuine open call open to non-members and any discipline. Amount unknown (uncertain).

title: Hakluyt Society Essay Prize
amount_raw: £1250 to the winning essay, with a second prize of £250 to the runner-up
eligibility_summary: Any registered graduate student at a higher education institution (university or equivalent), or anyone awarded a graduate degree in the past three years. Career-break allowances made. International entrants eligible (past winners from UK, US, Canada, Australia, etc.).
summary: Annual essay prize for an essay (6,000-8,000 words) based on original research in any humanities or social-science discipline on the history of travel, exploration and cultural encounter. Winners also receive a certificate, one-year Society membership and a volume; winning essays may be published.
